case_name: Mohammed Yusuf v Faij Mohammad and Others
facts: Appellant filed a suit for a decree for permanent injunction in 2002.
Summons upon the defendants were served on 6.7.2002.
Defendants appeared through their learned advocate on 19.7.2002.
Appellant filed an application for grant of temporary injunction which was rejected on 28.1.2004.
An appeal was preferred thereagainst which was disposed of by an order dated 14.5.2004.
On or about 31.1.2005, the appellant also filed an application before the learned trial Judge for pronouncing judgment in terms of Order 8 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
A Revision Petition was filed by the respondents which by reason of an order dated 29.8.2007 was dismissed by the learned District Judge.
issues: Whether the High Court committed a serious error in passing the impugned judgment?
Whether the defendants-respondents could file written statement after expiry of period of 90 days?
petitioner_arguments: The High Court committed a serious error in passing the impugned judgment.

Keeping in view the fact that the summons upon the defendants were served on 6.7.2002 and no step having been taken to file written statement for a period of three years and only on 31.5.2005, an application for filing written statement having been filed, the High Court committed a serious error in passing the impugned judgment.
respondent_arguments: From a perusal of the order-sheet before the trial Court, it would appear that dates after dates were fixed for filing written statement and, furthermore, having regard to the fact that the appellant himself preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge against an order rejecting his application for grant of temporary injunction, the written statement could not be filed.
court_reasoning: The provisions of Order 8 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure having been held to be directory in nature by this Court in Kailash Vs. Nanhku and Ors. - (2005) 4 SCC 480 2005 Indlaw SC 269, this Court may not exercise its discretionary jurisdiction u/art. 136 of the Constitution of India.

The grant of extension of time beyond 30 days is not automatic, that it should be exercised with caution and for adequate reasons and that an extension of time beyond 90 days of the service of summons must be granted only based on a clear satisfaction of the justification for granting such extension.
holding: The impugned judgment of the High Court cannot be sustained. It is set aside accordingly.
